title: Asymmetric cold-start penalty causing token-rate collapse
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Summary: Several customers (hosted + dedicated + private) reported a sudden collapse in tokens-per-second (sustained TPS drop) for short-lived sessions and bursty traffic. Symptoms: first-token latency spike followed by ~70% drop in steady-state token throughput for 10-30s after a cold allocation. This is reproducible on model variants with heterogeneous weight sizes (int8 vs fp16) and high-fanout routing. Impact: customer-facing escalations from 3 accounts, increased error-rate/latency alerts, and a few automated rollback events for Dedicated clusters.

Hypothesis: an asymmetric warmup/credit accounting bug in the warmstart allocator combined with an eager KV-prefetch that races kernel selection. The allocator aggressively charges warmup credits to the first few heavy-weight variants, starving subsequent warm-starts and causing the scheduler to fall back to conservative kernels that dramatically reduce token/sec.

Scope: Hosted API, Redwood Dedicated pools, and Private VPC deployments that use mixed-variant routing. Particularly visible under short session workloads (average 20-80 tokens) and when fanout > 3.

Goals:
- Patch hotfix to eliminate immediate customer pain (restore tokens/sec within SLA window).
- Add telemetry and rollout safety to prevent recurrence.
- Plan a durable redesign for the warmstart allocator to handle heterogenous weights fairly.
comments: 2026-03-10 — Initial triage: Aisha reproduced the drop locally with a short session harness and mixed-variant routing. Captured perf traces showing kernel fallback events at ~120ms and subsequent token-rate drop to ~30% of baseline.

2026-03-11 — Investigation: Marcos test revealed warmup_credit ledger shows negative transient credits for nodes serving heavy-variant requests. Conjecture: concurrent warmup allocation not accounting for per-variant weight normalization. Added temporary gauges to trace warm_credit per-variant.

2026-03-12 — Mitigation deployed (hotpatch v2.13.1): introduce conservative per-request warm-credit cap + emergency per-pool redistribution. Early signals: Hosted clusters recovered tokens/sec to ~90% baseline within 12m of rollout. Dedicated customer reported partial improvement on a canary pool.
2026-03-12 — Follow-up: Added fallback that routes small sessions to pre-warmed light variants when available. This reduced observed customer errors while we iterate on allocator fix.

2026-03-13 — Post-mortem notes: observed race between KV-prefetch completion and kernel selector causing eviction thrash. PV team proposed adding a pre-kernel lock for coldstart path to avoid thrash during warm-credit rebalancing.

2026-03-14 — Current: Working on PR to add 'warm_credit_smoothing' + per-variant weight normalization, and extended telemetry 'coldstart_penalty_ratio'. Plan A: apply allocator fix + canary in Hosted, then Dedicated. Plan B: if canary shows regressions, rollback allocator changes and use routing-based mitigation (prefer light variants).
2026-03-14 — Customer comms: Support sent interim mitigation steps and ETA for durable fix. CS scheduled follow-up with affected accounts on 2026-03-16.
